intro: Code Explained — real excerpts from MapSnap's source, each mapped to the feature it creates. MapSnap is a local-first schema-intelligence tool: one stdlib http.server module, an engine-agnostic extraction layer, a compliance-first egress guardrail, a 6-layer per-profile enrichment stack, and local-first AI (Ollama) with a guarded cloud escape hatch.

snippets.title: Bind to 127.0.0.1:9876 and serve
snippets.feature: The zero-framework local web server (no Flask/FastAPI)
snippets.code:
server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", args.port), Handler)
url    = f"http://localhost:{args.port}/"

print(f"==========================================")
print(f"  MapSnap  |  {url}")
print(f"==========================================")
...
if not args.no_browser:
    threading.Timer(0.8, lambda: webbrowser.open(url)).start()

try:
    server.serve_forever()
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("\nStopped.")
snippets.explanation: The entire app is one stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer bound to localhost only — no web framework, threaded so SSE streaming works. This is what keeps the install dependency-light and trivially portable to a customer or air-gapped box.

snippets.title: Path-based dispatch of ~50 /api/* routes
snippets.feature: The API surface that backs every tab in the HTML browser
snippets.explanation: do_GET / do_POST normalise the path then run a flat if/elif chain, dispatching each /api/* route to its handler. There is no router object — the dispatch table IS the if-chain, which keeps the single-file design honest and greppable.

snippets.title: SQLite schema extraction via PRAGMA
snippets.feature: Multi-engine extraction — one canonical schema.json per engine
snippets.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(self.file_path)
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
cur = conn.cursor()

cur.execute(
    "SELECT name, type FROM sqlite_master "
    "WHERE type IN ('table','view') ORDER BY name"
)
...
for obj_name, obj in objects_map.items():
    cur.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info(\"{obj_name}\")")
    for row in cur.fetchall():
        obj["columns"].append(_make_col(
            name=row["name"],
            data_type=(row["type"] or "text").lower(),
            is_pk=bool(row["pk"]),
            nullable=not row["notnull"],
            default=row["dflt_value"],
        ))
snippets.explanation: Each engine has its own extractor class, but all of them emit the SAME shape via the shared _make_object / _make_col / _make_schema helpers. SQLite reads sqlite_master + PRAGMA table_info / foreign_key_list; the result is one canonical schema.json the rest of MapSnap understands regardless of source engine.

snippets.title: PostgreSQL connect + information_schema pull
snippets.feature: Engine-agnostic live extract over Postgres / MySQL / Oracle
snippets.code:
try:
    import psycopg2
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: psycopg2 not installed. Run: pip install psycopg2-binary")
    sys.exit(1)

print(f"Connecting to PostgreSQL: {self.host}:{self.port}/{self.database}")
conn = psycopg2.connect(
    host=self.host, port=self.port, dbname=self.database,
    user=self.username, password=self.password, connect_timeout=15,
)
cur = conn.cursor()
...
rows = q("""
    SELECT t.table_schema, t.table_name, t.table_type
    FROM information_schema.tables t
    WHERE t.table_type IN ('BASE TABLE','VIEW')
    ...
""")
snippets.explanation: Postgres, MySQL and Oracle extractors each import their driver lazily (so the app ships thin and only pulls the driver a connection needs) and walk information_schema / ALL_TAB_COLUMNS. The MySQL and Oracle classes reuse PostgresExtractor._wire_fks to build the FK graph, so all relational engines converge on identical foreign_keys_in / foreign_keys_out.

snippets.title: Open a live connection per engine for queries
snippets.feature: One saved connection, five engines — SQL Server/SQLite/Postgres/MySQL/Oracle
snippets.code:
db_type = (conn.get("db_type") or "sqlserver").lower()
if db_type == "sqlserver":
    import pyodbc
    dsn = conn.get("dsn") or conn.get("connection_string", "")
    ...
    cx = pyodbc.connect(dsn, timeout=10)
    cx.timeout = 30                       # per-query timeout (seconds)
    return cx, db_type
if db_type == "sqlite":
    import sqlite3
    return sqlite3.connect(conn.get("file", "")), db_type
if db_type == "postgres":
    import psycopg2
    return psycopg2.connect(host=conn.get("host"), port=int(conn.get("port", 5432)),
        dbname=conn.get("database"), user=conn.get("username"),
        password=conn.get("password", ""), connect_timeout=10), db_type
if db_type == "mysql":
    import pymysql
    return pymysql.connect(...), db_type
if db_type == "oracle":
    import oracledb
    dsn_str = f"{conn.get('host')}:{conn.get('port', 1521)}/{conn.get('service', '')}"
    return oracledb.connect(user=conn.get("username"),
        password=conn.get("password", ""), dsn=dsn_str), db_type
raise RuntimeError(f"Live SQL not supported for db_type '{db_type}'.")
snippets.explanation: At query time the saved .mapsnap_conn.json's db_type selects the right DB-API driver — pyodbc (Trusted_Connection for Windows auth), sqlite3, psycopg2, pymysql, or oracledb thin mode — and returns a live connection the caller closes. This is the single point where 'which engine' becomes a concrete connection.

snippets.title: The single cloud-egress chokepoint
snippets.feature: Fail-safe compliance control plane (FERPA / GLBA / HIPAA)
snippets.code:
if policy is None:
    policy = resolve_data_policy(profile_folder, settings)
...
if not cloud_allowed(policy):
    reason = (
        f"Data policy for this profile is '{policy}' - cloud models are "
        f"blocked. Only local (Ollama) models may be used. ...")
    _log(f"GUARDRAIL block: cloud egress refused model={model} "
         f"policy={policy} folder={profile_folder}", "warning")
    return {"allowed": False, "policy": policy, "reason": reason,
            "messages": messages, "redacted": []}

# Cloud is permitted. First strip LOCAL_ONLY-wrapped spans (profiling
# sample VALUES) so they never leave, then scrub stray regulated VALUES.
stripped_local = False
pre = []
for m in messages:
    clean, removed = strip_local_only(m.get("content", ""))
    if removed:
        stripped_local = True
    nm = dict(m); nm["content"] = clean; pre.append(nm)
scrubbed, redacted = scrub_messages(pre)
snippets.explanation: Every cloud-model call passes through this one function. It resolves the per-profile data_policy (fail-safe local_only), BLOCKS the call outright when cloud is not allowed, strips local-only profiling samples, scrubs regulated values, and logs an auditable decision. Local Ollama and local SQL execution never call it, so they are never touched.

snippets.title: Fail-safe policy resolution
snippets.feature: Compliant-by-default posture — unknown means local_only
snippets.explanation: Policy comes from the per-profile mapsnap_meta.json, else the global default, else the hard-coded DEFAULT_POLICY = 'local_only'. Any unset/unknown/corrupt value collapses to local_only, so a profile is compliant before anyone configures it — the safe state is the default, not a retrofit.

snippets.title: Value-level PII detection + local-only sentinel
snippets.feature: Regulated-value scrubbing and profiling-sample withholding
snippets.explanation: scrub_text redacts SSN / email / phone / card-number value patterns from any outbound payload (schema/metadata text doesn't match, so it's untouched). strip_local_only removes any span the prompt-builder wrapped in the [[MAPSNAP_LOCAL_ONLY]] sentinel — the Layer-4 sample VALUES — so profiling data physically cannot reach a cloud model.

snippets.title: Local Ollama streaming (default path)
snippets.feature: Local-first chat + NL→SQL — no data leaves the box
snippets.code:
p    = urllib.parse.urlparse(ollama_url)
# Generous timeout: a large model cold-loading from disk plus prompt-eval
# over a big schema can take minutes. The SSE keepalive thread holds the
# client connection open meanwhile.
conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(
    p.hostname or "localhost", p.port or 11434, timeout=600)
conn.request("POST", endpoint, body=ollama_body,
             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                      "Content-Length": str(len(ollama_body))})
resp = conn.getresponse()
...
msg = chunk.get("message") or {}
think = msg.get("thinking") or ""
if think:
    sse("thinking", {"text": think})
snippets.explanation: The default model call goes to local Ollama on :11434 via /api/chat or /api/generate and is streamed to the browser as Server-Sent Events. A background keepalive thread prevents proxy idle-timeouts, and reasoning models' separate 'thinking' field is forwarded as its own event so the UI shows 'Reasoning…' instead of looking hung. This path never passes through the guardrail — it stays on-box.

snippets.title: OpenRouter cloud streaming (escape hatch)
snippets.feature: Optional frontier-model access, OpenAI-compatible SSE
snippets.code:
body = json.dumps({"model": model, "messages": messages, "stream": True}).encode("utf-8")
conn = _hc.HTTPSConnection("openrouter.ai", 443, timeout=600)
conn.request("POST", "/api/v1/chat/completions", body=body, headers={
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
    "Content-Type":  "application/json",
    "HTTP-Referer":  "https://mapsnap.local",
    "X-Title":       "MapSnap",
})
resp = conn.getresponse()
...
while True:
    line = resp.readline()
    if not line: break
    line = line.strip()
    if not line or not line.startswith(b"data:"): continue
    payload = line[5:].strip()
    if payload == b"[DONE]": break
    chunk = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
    token = (chunk["choices"][0].get("delta") or {}).get("content") or ""
    if token:
        sse("token", {"text": token})
snippets.explanation: When (and only when) the guardrail has allowed it, cloud calls go to OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible /api/v1/chat/completions and parse 'data:' SSE delta lines into the same token/done/error events as the local path — so the UI is identical whether the model is local or cloud.

snippets.title: Guardrail wraps the cloud call in /api/chat
snippets.feature: Egress enforcement wired into the chat pipeline
snippets.explanation: Only the is_cloud branch invokes the guardrail. A blocked decision short-circuits with the policy reason; an allowed decision swaps in the scrubbed messages and emits a 'guardrail' event so the UI can show what was redacted. This is the integration point that makes 'use a frontier model' and 'choose what may leave' the same deliberate decision.

snippets.title: Natural-language question to read-only SQL
snippets.feature: The NL→SQL assistant over the per-profile schema
snippets.code:
schema = json.loads(sf.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
tables = find_relevant_tables(schema, question, max_tables=8)
# Hybrid retrieval (Layer 5): augment keyword tables with semantic
# (meaning) matches so NL->SQL sees the right tables even when the
# question words don't appear in any table name. Best-effort.
tables = _interleave_unique(
    [], tables, _semantic_objects(schema, question, sf.parent, k=5),
    cap=10)
ddl    = _fmt_ddl(tables)
dialect = (schema.get("metadata", {}).get("db_type") or "sqlserver")
...
prompt = (
    "### Task\n"
    f"Generate a single read-only {dialect} SELECT query to answer "
    f"[QUESTION]{question}[/QUESTION]\n\n"
    "### Database Schema\n"
    f"{ddl}\n\n"
    + ex_block + ann_block + prof_block + onbase_hint +
    "### Rules\n"
    "- Output ONLY the SQL, no prose, no markdown fences.\n"
    "- SELECT only; never modify data.\n")
snippets.explanation: NL→SQL picks the relevant tables (keyword + semantic, see Layer 5), renders their DDL, and builds a dialect-aware prompt (the model defaults to sqlcoder via Ollama /api/generate). The prompt is enriched with worked examples (ex_block), annotations and profiling, and explicitly constrains the model to a single read-only SELECT.

snippets.title: The enrichment layer registry
snippets.feature: 'Born understood' — schemas auto-enriched on extract/import
snippets.explanation: The enrichment stack is data-driven: each layer declares the sidecar it produces, whether it needs a live connection, whether it may use a cloud model, and the tool that implements it. enrich.py reads this registry to know what can run — adding a layer is a registry entry plus a tool, not orchestration surgery.

snippets.title: Gated, idempotent, best-effort layer runner
snippets.feature: Enrichment that never breaks a build
snippets.explanation: Each layer passes five gates — system applicability, the per-profile enable grid, live-connection need, source-hash idempotency, then a try/except run. A layer failure is logged and skipped; enrichment is best-effort and always exits 0, so it can run inline on every extract / doc-import / config-import without ever blocking the build.

snippets.title: Read-only, PII-masked data profiling (Layer 4)
snippets.feature: Real-sample column profiling with auto PII classification
snippets.code:
DEFAULT_MAX_TABLES = 250
DEFAULT_SAMPLE = 25          # rows pulled per table
MAX_SAMPLE = 1000            # hard cap, matches run-sql
SAMPLE_VALUES_KEPT = 8       # distinct sample values stored per column
LOOKUP_ROW_CEILING = 500     # a small reference table is a "lookup"

# Binary / BLOB / opaque types never pulled over the wire.
_BLOB_HINTS = (
    "binary", "image", "blob", "bytea", "raw", "geography", "geometry",
    "hierarchyid", "sql_variant", "rowversion", "timestamp",
    "clob", "nclob", "xml",
)

import guardrail  # portable PII masking (scrub_text) + classifications
snippets.explanation: Layer 4 reads ACTUAL data in place — one capped SELECT sample plus a COUNT(*) per table, read-only, never selecting BLOB/binary columns. It auto-detects PII classes (SSN/email/phone/DOB/name/account) and writes them to mapsnap_meta.json so the guardrail can mask them, and it masks samples via the shared guardrail before they ever land in profile.json.

snippets.title: One local embedding per table (Layer 5 build)
snippets.feature: Meaning-based table retrieval — 'checks' finds doctype/itemdata
snippets.code:
def _embed(texts, *, ollama_url=OLLAMA_URL, model=EMBED_MODEL, timeout=120):
    """Embed a list of strings via Ollama /api/embed (batched)."""
    out = []
    for i in range(0, len(texts), EMBED_BATCH):
        chunk = texts[i:i + EMBED_BATCH]
        body = json.dumps({"model": model, "input": chunk}).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(ollama_url + "/api/embed", data=body,
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
            data = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
        out.extend(data.get("embeddings") or [])
    return out
...
import chromadb
client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=str(idx_path))
col = client.create_collection(COLLECTION, metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})
col.add(ids=ids[i:i + 2000], embeddings=vectors[i:i + 2000],
        documents=docs[i:i + 2000])
snippets.explanation: Each table is turned into one synthesized document (name + purpose + columns + masked samples + business names) and embedded with the LOCAL nomic-embed-text model via Ollama, then stored in a per-profile ChromaDB .index/. Because vectors can encode sample values, keeping both the embed model and the store local means they never leave the box. The build is source-hash-gated so a fresh index is skipped.

snippets.title: Semantic query with graceful keyword fallback
snippets.feature: Hybrid retrieval that degrades to keyword when Ollama is down
snippets.explanation: At query time the question is embedded and matched against the index, returning [(table, score)] for the closest tables by meaning. Any failure — no index, Ollama down — returns [] so the caller silently falls back to pure keyword retrieval, which is why the assistant stays useful even with no GPU or no embeddings built.

snippets.title: Server-side interleave of keyword + semantic hits
snippets.feature: The hybrid retriever the NL→SQL and chat prompts consume
snippets.explanation: The server maps semantic_index.query's table names back to full schema objects, drops junk tables and anything not in this schema, and hands them to _interleave_unique so keyword matches and meaning matches are merged into one capped table set. This is the bridge between the vector index and the prompt builders.

snippets.title: Read-only SELECT guard
snippets.feature: SQL safety — only a single SELECT runs, against the live DB
snippets.code:
_SQL_FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"\b(insert|update|delete|drop|alter|create|truncate|merge|grant|revoke|"
    r"exec|execute|sp_\w+|xp_\w+|into|bulk|shutdown|waitfor|backup|restore|"
    r"reconfigure|openquery|openrowset)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

def validate_readonly_sql(sql: str):
    ...
    # strip /* */ and -- comments so keywords can't hide in them
    s = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", " ", sql, flags=re.S)
    s = re.sub(r"--[^\n]*", " ", s)
    s = s.strip().rstrip(";").strip()
    if ";" in s:
        return False, "Only a single statement is allowed (no ';')."
    low = s.lower()
    if not (low.startswith("select") or low.startswith("with")):
        return False, "Only SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) queries are allowed."
    m = _SQL_FORBIDDEN.search(low)
    if m:
        return False, f"Keyword '{m.group(1)}' is not allowed (read-only mode)."
    return True, s
snippets.explanation: Before any model-written or user-written SQL touches the database, it is stripped of comments, forced to a single statement, required to begin with SELECT/WITH, and screened against a forbidden-keyword list. This guard is what lets MapSnap run AI-generated SQL against a real production database without risk of mutation.

snippets.title: Execute locally, cap rows, record verified pairs
snippets.feature: Local query execution that never leaves the box

if not ok_sql:

conn_file = PRODUCT_DIR / folder / ".mapsnap_conn.json"
...

cx, db_type = _open_saved_sql_conn(conn)
cur = cx.cursor()
cur.execute(cleaned)
columns = [d[0] for d in cur.description] if cur.description else []
fetched = cur.fetchmany(limit_n)
truncated = bool(cur.fetchone())     # was there at least one more row?

...

snippets.explanation: /api/run-sql validates the SQL, opens the profile's saved live connection (any engine), executes, and fetches at most limit_n rows (hard-capped at 1000) with a truncation flag. Execution is entirely local — results never go to a cloud model. When the query came from an NL question, the (question, SQL) pair is recorded as a verified few-shot example.

snippets.title: SQLite users + sessions schema
snippets.feature: The login-mode account store (mapsnap_users.db)
snippets.code:
c.executescript("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
        id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        username        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
        password_hash   TEXT NOT NULL,
        role            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewer',
        tabs_override   TEXT,
        must_change_pw  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        created_at      TEXT NOT NULL
    );
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
        token       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
        expires_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
        FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    );
""")
cols = [r["name"] for r in c.execute("PRAGMA table_info(users)").fetchall()]
if "features_override" not in cols:
    c.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN features_override TEXT")
snippets.explanation: The only SQLite database MapSnap owns is the app store: users and sessions. Sessions are opaque tokens with a 7-day expiry and a cascade delete on the owning user. The inline ALTER migration adds feature-level permissions to older DBs without a migration tool — fitting the dependency-light design.

snippets.title: PBKDF2 password hashing
snippets.feature: Secure credential storage for ship-mode login
snippets.explanation: Passwords are stored as salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 200k iterations (OWASP 2023 minimum), self-describing so the iteration count can rise later. Verification uses hmac.compare_digest for constant-time comparison. All of this is stdlib — no crypto dependency to ship.

snippets.title: Session resolution on each request
snippets.feature: Login-mode auth gate over the /api/* surface
snippets.explanation: On each request the server reads the mapsnap_session cookie, looks up the live session, and resolves the user's role / tabs / features. Two modes coexist: 'login' (real accounts, ship-mode) and 'os_user' (role from %USERNAME%, dev box). The do_GET/do_POST auth gate uses this to block the /api/* surface for visitors without a valid session.
